A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-J are readable and support comparison, including the additional material in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPD-distance simulations, classification experiments on four datasets, and power and backbone ablations in Figure 1 and Tables 3, 5, and 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds transformer experiments and bias-reformulation ablations in Tables 11 and 12.

M1.justification: The main GCP pipeline and existing classifiers remain unchanged. Appendix H.4 introduces the experimental variant Pow-EMLR', replacing separate scalar biases with inner products against a shared symmetric matrix P. This changes the variant's parameterization without replacing the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k, Birds, Cars, Aircrafts, and the same synthetic SPD-distance scenario. The added transformer and bias experiments reuse existing datasets and classification tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds ScalePow-EMLR to Table 6a's power comparisons, where v1 compared only Pow-EMLR and Pow-TMLR. Table 12 introduces Pow-EMLR' against those existing classifiers. Table 5's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H.3 extends evaluation to SoT-7, trained for up to 250 epochs with batch size 512. Existing reported settings also change: Pow-TMLR's Cars batch size changes from 6 to 10, and the Pow-/ScalePow-EMLR Birds/Cars learning-rate reduction changes from division by 10 to division by 5. These establish substantial protocol additions and reported revisions, without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 tests the Pow-/ScalePow equivalence across additional powers, adds a transformer backbone check, and examines bias reformulation across all three FGVC datasets. Figure 3 revises the Birds training-dynamics evidence. Conversely, Section 6.2 removes v1's observation that Pow-TMLR fails to converge with AlexNet plus batch normalization.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 1's 335.84 ± 1.61 summary for 1,000 random SPD pairs. Neither reports classification seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6a revises multiple scores and adds ScalePow-EMLR rows. For example, Cars Pow-TMLR at power 0.5 changes from 35.41/58.95 to 55.01/77.95 top-1/top-5 accuracy. Tables 11 and 12 add transformer and shared-bias results, and Figure 3 changes the Birds trajectory. Tables 3, 5, and 6b retain their scores. The numerical revisions are not explained sufficiently to establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Theorem 2, its supporting proofs, and the negative-power extension are retained. Appendix G.3 adds the mathematical assertion that fixing all P_k to I in Equation 16 recovers Pow-TMLR, while H.4 introduces the shared-P restriction. The new special-case assertion does not address the unrestricted FC bias in the original tangent-classifier definition.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that matrix-function normalization is explained by implicit Riemannian classifiers rather than tangent classifiers, supported by large-scale and fine-grained classification experiments. v3 highlights the 'first intrinsic explanation' in the introduction, but this novelty claim already appears in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix G.3 newly argues that tangent classifiers are restricted special cases of Riemannian classifiers, adding an expressivity rationale. H.4 explains the computational motivation for sharing P across classes. The main PEM-versus-LEM interpretation and Appendix A's computational limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link and Table 10's systematic hyperparameter documentation, including previously unstated ImageNet training duration, batch size, and scheduler milestones, plus several FGVC batch sizes. It also supplies the SoT-7 training budget and shared-P implementation rationale. This substantially expands reproducibility information beyond v1's prose settings and baseline-code reference.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix B add references on higher-order pooling, graph pooling, product geometries, and other manifold networks; the new experiments cite SoT and hyperbolic bias reformulations. The paper retains its positioning as a geometric explanation of GCP rather than a state-of-the-art performance method.

P1.justification: v3 polishes prose, emphasizes contribution headings, updates publication and affiliation text, and adds acknowledgments and subsections G.3, H.3, and H.4. The main seven-section narrative and overall appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 transposes and reformats Table 4, expands Table 6a, reformats Table 9, and adds Tables 10-12. Figure 3 is enlarged and its Birds panel revised, including a shorter displayed epoch range. These substantially change the presentation of theory, settings, and empirical evidence.

improvement.justification: The transformer and bias controls, extended power ablation, and clearer reproduction settings modestly strengthen validation and transparency. The gains are limited by absent classification uncertainty estimates, unexplained Table 6 revisions, and removal of the AlexNet-plus-BN failure observation. Appendix G.3 also adds an unqualified special-case argument without resolving the FC-bias issue. Overall, the added empirical checks and documentation provide a limited net improvement.
